Bench: Prakash Chandra Gupta  1   IN THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT INDORE  BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA  ON THE 13th OF AUGUST, 2024  MISC. CRIMINAL CASE No. 23515 of 2024  VISHNU DANGI  Versus  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH  Appearance:
 Shri Girish Desai, learned counsel for the applicant.
 Shri Hemant Sharma, learned G.A. for the State.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT INDORE
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: ORDER Heard with the aid of case diary.

This is repeat third bail application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail to the applicant/accused, relating to FIR/Crime No.84/2022, dated (not mentioned) registered at Police Station-Tilak Nagar, District- Indore (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 420, 406, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of IPC and he is in custody since 07.02.2023.

2. His first and second bail application were dismissed on merit vide order dated 13.07.2023 passed by this Court in M.Cr.C. No.22317/2023 and order dated 16.02.2024 passed in M.Cr.C.
No.1809/2024.

3. Prosecution story begins with sale agreement of agricultural land in favour of Atul Agrawal with his attorney, Kapil Agrawal, bearing survey No.670/13 having area of 0.918 Hectare with Vishnu Dhangi on 09.01.2017 for a consideration of Rs.66,00,000/-, which was paid by the complainant.
The accused kept on avoiding the execution of sale deed in favour of complainant.
Later on, when the complainant sought information, he came to know that the aforesaid land has already been sold to Karls Real Estate Pvt. Ltd. through director Hullash Jain on 12.12.2011.

It has also been alleged by the complainant that present applicant and co-accused Hullash Jain entered into criminal conspiracy and in furtherance of which has also sold the aforesaid land to Rakesh Yadav on 20.02.2018 in which Hullash Jain has signed the sale deed as a witness, being well versed with the aforesaid fact.

Applicant and co-accused, Hullash Jain have Vishnu Dangi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46530209/
1 wrongfully gained and caused wrongful loss to the complainant.

sentences.text: Complaint of the aforesaid matter was made to police and an FIR was registered on 15.03.2022 at police station Tilak Nagar, Indore.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant/accused submits that the applicant has not committed the offence and has falsely been implicated in the case.

After dismissal of earlier bail applications of the applicants on merits complainant Atul (P.W.-3), material witnesses Kapil (P.W.-1) and Hukumchand (P.W.-4) have been examined before the trial court but they are completely turned hostile and have not supported the case of the prosecution.
Applicant is in custody since 07.02.2023.
Conclusion of trial will take sufficient long time for its disposal therefore, it is prayed that under the changed circumstances applicant be released on bail.
5. On the other hand, learned G.A. for the State opposed the prayer of the applicant and prayed for its rejection.

6. Having considered the submissions advanced from counsel for the 3 MCRC-23515-2024 parties,
this Court is of the view that in the changed circumstances applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
Hence, the bail application is allowed.

7. It is directed that the applicant-VISHNU DANGI be released on bail upon his/her furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for his/her appearance before the trial Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the trial Court during pendency of the trial.
It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
8. M.Cr.C. stands disposed of, accordingly.
C.c. as per rules.

(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE ajit Vishnu Dangi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46530209/
